subject.title: fix: verify provider ownership before cloud cleanup

question: Should this security hardening intentionally fail closed for legacy Azure leases and deferred cleanup records that lack persisted providerScope, or should the PR include a migration/operator recovery path before merge?
rationale: The fail-closed behavior matches the documented destructive-provider boundary, but it intentionally changes upgrade cleanup behavior for already-stored Azure records and needs maintainer ownership before landing.

options.title: Accept Fail-Closed With Proof
options.body: Merge after AWS and Azure live zero-residue proof is attached and the legacy unscoped Azure cleanup behavior is explicitly accepted as manual resolution.

options.title: Require Recovery Path First
options.body: Ask for a narrow migration, doctor, or operator recovery surface before fail-closing legacy Azure cleanup records in production.

options.title: Split Provider Landing
options.body: Land the lower-risk provider portions separately and keep Azure legacy cleanup semantics under a focused follow-up decision.

recommendation.title: Accept Fail-Closed With Proof
recommendation.body: Merge after AWS and Azure live zero-residue proof is attached and the legacy unscoped Azure cleanup behavior is explicitly accepted as manual resolution.
